title: Pre-Lesson C
subtitle: Hajimemashite — First Meeting
objectives: Introduce yourself with Hajimemashite, (name) to moushimasu, Yoroshiku onegai shimasu
Ask and answer about age: Nansai desu ka / (years) sai desu
Know the irregular age forms: issai, hassai, jussai, hatachi
Ask how old someone looks: Nansai ni miemasu ka

vocab.english: Nice to meet you / How do you do?

vocab.japanese: よろしくおねがいします
vocab.english: Best regards / I look forward to working with you

vocab.japanese: なんさいにみえますか
おなまえはなんですか

grammar.title: The first-meeting script
grammar.pattern: Hajimemashite. (name) to moushimasu. Yoroshiku onegai shimasu.
grammar.explanation: The standard self-introduction: 'Nice to meet you. I am called (name). Best regards.' Moushimasu is humble and polite. Say hajimemashite like 'hajimemashte' - the i in mashite is nearly silent.

examples.japanese: はじめまして。スミスともうします。
examples.english: Nice to meet you. I am Smith.

mistakes: Using hajimemashite with someone you already know - it is only for first meetings

grammar.title: Asking and telling age
grammar.explanation: Sai literally means 'years old' and always comes after the number. Some ages have irregular forms: issai (1), hassai (8), jussai (10, 30, 40, 50...), hatachi (20), juu issai (11), ni juu issai (21).
mistakes: Saying 'kusai' for 9 years old - kusai means smelly! Use kyuu sai

grammar.title: How old do I look?
grammar.pattern: Nansai ni miemasu ka / (number) sai ni miemasu
grammar.explanation: A friendly ice-breaker: 'How old do I look?' Answer with (number) sai ni miemasu - 'You look (number) years old.'

grammar.title: My name is... the natural way
grammar.pattern: (O)namae wa nan desu ka → (name) to moushimasu
grammar.explanation: Watashi no namae wa (name) desu is grammatically correct but not common between Japanese people. The natural reply to 'What is your name?' is (name) to moushimasu.
mistakes: Overusing 'watashi no namae wa ... desu' in natural conversation

exercises.prompt: When is hajimemashite used?
choices: Only when meeting someone for the first time
exercises.explanation: Hajimemashite is only for first meetings.

exercises.prompt: Hajimemashite. Sumisu ___ moushimasu.
exercises.explanation: The pattern is (name) TO moushimasu - 'I am called (name)'.

exercises.prompt: よろしくおねがいします
choices: Best regards / I look forward to working with you
exercises.explanation: A multi-purpose phrase with no exact English equivalent - here it means 'let's be nice to each other'.

exercises.prompt: なんさいですか
exercises.explanation: Nansai desu ka = How old are you?

exercises.prompt: I am 25 years old: Ni juu go ___ desu.
exercises.explanation: sai = years old; it always follows the number.

exercises.prompt: 1 year old in Japanese is...
exercises.explanation: 1 year old is irregular: issai.

exercises.prompt: 8 years old in Japanese is...
exercises.explanation: 8 years old is irregular: hassai.

exercises.prompt: 20 years old in Japanese is...
exercises.explanation: 20 is special: hatachi.

exercises.prompt: Why is 'kusai' wrong for 9 years old?
choices: It is rude for numbers over 5
exercises.explanation: Kusai means 'smelly'! Use kyuu sai.

exercises.prompt: 10 years old in Japanese is ___ (roomaji).
exercises.explanation: 10 is irregular: jussai (never 'juu sai'). 30, 40, 50 follow: san jussai, yon jussai, go jussai.

exercises.prompt: なんさいにみえますか
exercises.explanation: Nansai ni miemasu ka = How old do I look?

exercises.prompt: Ms. Hayashi says 'Hatachi ni miemasu.' What did she ask first?
exercises.explanation: From Conversation 3: she first asked 'How old do I look?' after Mr. Smith asked her age.

exercises.prompt: おなまえはなんですか
exercises.explanation: (O)namae wa nan desu ka = What is your name?

exercises.prompt: The NATURAL way to answer 'What is your name?' is...
choices: Watashi no namae wa Sumisu desu
exercises.explanation: The book says (name) to moushimasu is the natural way; 'watashi no namae wa...' is grammatically correct but uncommon.

exercises.prompt: Build the introduction 'Nice to meet you. I am Mori.':
exercises.explanation: Hajimemashite + (name) + to + moushimasu.

exercises.prompt: 15 years old: ___ (roomaji, e.g. from Pre-Lesson B + sai)
exercises.explanation: juu go (15) + sai = juu go sai.

exercises.prompt: How deep is a standard first-meeting bow?
choices: About 30 degrees, held about two seconds
exercises.explanation: A 30-degree bow held about two seconds is standard for first meetings; 15 degrees is the everyday bow.

exercises.prompt: Pronunciation note: hajimemashite sounds like...
exercises.explanation: The i in 'mashite' is silent - say 'hajimemashte'.

exercises.prompt: Type 'I am 20 years old' in roomaji (use the special 20-year-old word):
exercises.explanation: Hatachi desu - 20 uses the special word hatachi.

exercises.prompt: Match the age with its reading:
exercises.explanation: The four irregular ages.

quiz.prompt: Which reply answers 'Nansai ni miemasu ka'?
quiz.explanation: '(number) sai ni miemasu' answers 'How old do I look?'

quiz.prompt: Watashi no namae wa Sumisu desu is...
quiz.explanation: It is correct but (name) to moushimasu is what Japanese people actually say.

quiz.prompt: The everyday informal bow is about ___ degrees.
quiz.explanation: 15 degrees for everyday bows; 30 for first meetings.

summary: First-meeting script: Hajimemashite (say 'hajimemashte') → (name) to moushimasu → Yoroshiku onegai shimasu. Age: Nansai desu ka → (number) sai desu, with irregulars issai, hassai, jussai, hatachi. Fun icebreaker: Nansai ni miemasu ka.
